overall: Licences were accurate on both sides: every Commons file existed with the stated licence and author, the museum records (AIC, Met, Cleveland, SAAM) all confirmed public domain or CC0, and both flagged share-alike and personality-rights caveats; no wrong 'yes' was found, the weakest point being X's third-party-sourced salmon photo still marked 'yes'. The two often converged on the same image (Watoto choir, Ford salmon haul, Homer, Turner), so several briefs were decided by the second pick. Y more often chose the most literal, instantly readable metaphor (Hobbema avenue, river confluences, Whistler nocturne, odd-one-out grid), while X won where it found on-subject photos or paintings (lighthouse beam, Lagos traffic, Webster's choir, telescopes). Both sometimes described images inaccurately when checked (X's Hammershoi 'empty left half' and 'dark' loaf; Y's 'mostly black' Redon), so layout claims in the 'why' text should not be trusted without a look.
